primitives.name: number
primitives.about: A value in a range: a slider, with the value shown beside it; tap the value to type one.
primitives.fields: `value` within `min`..=`max`; `step` snaps it (`null`: continuous); `scale: "log"` spreads the slider by ratio, for a wide range such as a brush size (needs `min` above 0; left out, the slider is linear); `unit` is `none`, `percent` (a 0..=1 value shown as 0–100 %), `pixels` or `degrees`; `enabled: false` greys it out. Values and edits are in the number's own units whatever the scale.
primitives.sends: `number` edits: `begin`, `change` while dragging, then `commit` (or `cancel`); a typed value is one `commit`.

primitives.name: choice
primitives.about: One of several options: segmented for up to 4, a menu for more.
primitives.fields: `value` is the chosen option's `id`; option ids are unique; `enabled: false` greys it out.

primitives.name: section
primitives.about: A titled group of other nodes; the user can collapse it.
primitives.fields: `children` are any nodes; `collapsed` is how it starts.
primitives.sends: nothing itself; its children send their own edits.

primitives.name: item_list
primitives.about: Rows of items such as layers, top to bottom: tap to select, swipe to hide, long-press to rename, drag to reorder. Select in the header picks several rows, tap by tap, until Done; with a keyboard, Shift-tap selects a range and Command-tap adds or removes a row.
primitives.fields: each row's `id` is the app's own and unique in the list; `depth` indents it (inside groups); `visible: null` means it can't be hidden; `reorderable` allows dragging.
primitives.sends: `select`, `set_visible`, `rename` and (when reorderable) `move` edits, each one `commit`, naming rows by their `id`. A `select` has a `mode`: `replace` (a plain tap; also when left out), `toggle` (add the row or take it out) or `range` (from the last row selected to this one). A `move` names the row dragged; an app moves the whole selection when that row is one of several selected.

primitives.name: tool_palette
primitives.about: The app's tools, in a panel with the `rail` role: a vertical Liquid Glass rail at the canvas's leading edge. Tap a tool to select it; long-press a slot (a small corner mark says it has more) for its flyout of the other tools; double-tap the selected tool, or the rail's options button, for its options.
primitives.fields: `slots`, top to bottom, each with `tools`: the slot shows the selected tool when it holds it, else its first. A tool has an `id` (unique in the palette), a `label`, an `icon` (`symbol`, an SF Symbol name; `letter`, shown when the platform has no such symbol; the label's first letter when neither works) and a `shortcut` or `null`. `selected` is one of the tools. `options` names the app's Tool panel for the selected tool's options; without one, `fallback_options` is a command that shows them the app's own way; both `null`: no options.
primitives.sends: one `choice` edit with the tool's `id`, `commit`, when a tool is tapped or picked from a flyout. Options open the `options` panel as a popover from the rail, or send `{"action":"command","id":…}` with `fallback_options`.

chrome.name: menu_bar
chrome.about: The app's menus, in the iPad menu bar (pointer at the top edge, or hold ⌘) and a toolbar menu for touch. `Platform::set_menu` sends it whenever it changes (request kind 15), and again when the shell restarts.
chrome.fields: `menus`, left to right, each a `title`, a `role` and `items`. The `role` (`file`, `edit`, `view`, `window` or `help`; `null` or left out for a menu of the app's own) says which system menu it takes the place of, matched by role and never by its translated title; Window keeps the system's window items after the app's. An item is a `command` (an `id` unique in the whole bar, a `label`, a `shortcut` in the portable form such as `Cmd+Shift+Z` or `null`, `enabled`, and `checked`: `true` or `false` for a check mark, `null` for none), a `separator`, or a `submenu` with a `label` and `items`. Labels are never empty. A shortcut's modifiers are `Ctrl`, `Cmd`, `Alt` and `Shift` (`Ctrl` is the Control key, not ⌘), then one key: a character or a named key (`Enter`, `Tab`, `ArrowUp`, `F5`).
chrome.sends: a `command` with the item's `id` when the user picks an item without a shortcut; a `shortcut` with its `keys` when the item has one, or the keys are pressed on a hardware keyboard, so the app's own key handling decides, as for the key itself. Enabled and checked are read when a menu opens, so changing them alone redraws nothing.

chrome.name: status
chrome.about: What the app is telling the user: a message as a transient toast at the top (red for an error), and a long job as a progress capsule with a Cancel button. `Platform::set_status` sends it whenever it changes (request kind 16), and again when the shell restarts.
chrome.fields: `message` (`null` for none): its `text`, its `tone` (`info` or `error`) and an `id` (0 when left out). A message shows when its text, tone or id changes; give each new message a new id (`Status::message_id`) so the same text said again shows again. `progress` (`null` for none): a `label`, a `fraction` from 0 to 1 (`null` while unknown) and `cancel`, a command id or `null` for a job that can't be stopped.
chrome.sends: the `cancel` command when the user taps Cancel.
